citation: Schalk G, McFarland DJ, Hinterberger T, Birbaumer N, Wolpaw JR. BCI2000: a general-purpose brain-computer interface (BCI) system. IEEE Trans Biomed Eng 2004;51(6):1034-1043. EEG Motor Movement/Imagery Database, PhysioNet (Goldberger et al. 2000).
record_used: subject S002, baseline run R02 (eyes-closed), the eight parieto-occipital channels (PO7, PO3, POz, PO4, PO8, O1, Oz, O2), first 10 s at 160 Hz -- subset from the SAME git-tracked 64-channel root the Welch/Hjorth/spectrogram cases use.
pipeline: readRDS(eeg8post_s002r02) -> PhysioEEG::eegCoherence(method='coherence', window_sec=2, overlap=0.5, band=c(8,13)): the pairwise magnitude-squared coherence matrix, band-averaged over the alpha band. The reference re-computes the matrix with scipy.signal.coherence (symmetric Hann, matched window length + overlap, detrend=False) over the identical band, via reticulate. Deterministic.
note: The root is the eight parieto-occipital channels of the eyes-closed EEG, subset from agent/eval/data/hjorth-eeg/eeg64_s002r02.rds. Magnitude-squared coherence Cxy = |Sxy|^2/(Sxx*Syy) measures frequency-resolved linear coupling. This is the FIRST external-reference (scipy) certification of eegCoherence (previously 'golden' internal only). eegCoherence reproduces scipy.signal.coherence BIT-FOR-BIT (max |diff| ~2e-16 over all 28 pairs) once the conventions are matched: symmetric Hann window, matched window length (round(window_sec*sr), forced even) + hop, detrend=False -- and because the coherence RATIO cancels the window normalization, the match is machine epsilon. The finding: posterior alpha coherence is high (mean 0.63, peaking 0.90 between adjacent occipital channels PO3-O1) -- the eyes-closed alpha rhythm is spatially synchronized across the parieto-occipital region, cross-consistent with the Welch (high posterior alpha power), spectrogram (sustained alpha), and Hjorth (low posterior mobility) cases on the SAME data. CAVEAT: magnitude-squared coherence is inflated by volume conduction (a shared source projects to nearby electrodes at zero lag), so high coherence is not proof of true cortico-cortical coupling; the op also offers imaginary coherence (method='imaginary') which suppresses the zero-lag component.
